system_type_reason: Deployable browser control-plane service with its own built-in agent loop for MCP clients and operators.

repo_overview.summary: MCP-native browser control plane: a FastAPI controller manages Playwright browser sessions (screenshots, DOM summaries, OCR, actions) for external MCP clients and REST callers. It also ships a built-in agent loop (OpenAI/Claude/Gemini adapters) that observes the page, lets the LLM pick one browser action, executes it and repeats until done, human takeover or max_steps. Around this sits operator infrastructure: approvals, noVNC human takeover, audit and Witness receipts, PII scrubbing, per-session container isolation.

components.purpose: agent control flow: observe/decide/execute step and multi-step run loop, persistent job queue with checkpoints, resume and cancel
LLM adapters (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini) and shared base: prompt building, decision parsing, provider API errors
session lifecycle, action execution, observation, human takeover, approvals, auth profiles, diagnostics, bot-challenge detection
action execution pipeline, action error classes, vision-based target resolution
governance: approval gates, runtime policy, compliance presets, request rate limits, PII scrubbing
audit trail, hash-chained Witness receipts, event bus, metrics
MCP server, tool registry and tool packs (curated/full profiles), tool input validation
convergence harness: runs task contracts, records traces, verifies completion, drift monitor, induces staged skill candidates
deterministic DAG workflow engine with per-step retry, scheduled jobs
signed capability delegation (tool/session/workflow) to peer auto-browser nodes
per-session browser containers, session persistence, orphan cleanup, readiness checks
fingerprint and humanizer, proxy personas, session memory injected into the goal, DOM pruning
browser container image with noVNC, reverse SSH tunnel
Python SDK, MCP stdio bridge, LangChain/CrewAI adapters
fixture evals, benchmark adapters, smoke/doctor scripts, tests

resilience.name: low-progress loop guard with human takeover
resilience.what_it_is: After each step, the last 3 steps are checked: if all are 'acted', all are low-progress (verification.verified is False, or url, title and text_excerpt are unchanged before/after) and share one identical action signature (action, element_id, selector, url, text, key, deltas, wait_ms), the orchestrator calls request_human_takeover and ends the run with status 'takeover'.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in orchestrator.run after every step. Detects the agent repeating the same ineffective browser action and hands the live session to a human operator. Otherwise the agent burns its whole step budget on an identical no-op action.

resilience.name: job step checkpointing and resume with resume context
resilience.what_it_is: Background agent_run jobs persist a checkpoint per step to a JSON job file. On controller restart, running jobs are marked 'interrupted' and queued jobs are re-enqueued. resume_job restarts failed, interrupted, max_steps_reached, approval_required or error runs with the remaining step budget and injects a resume context (last 6 checkpoints plus an instruction to avoid repeating completed actions) into context_hints.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps orchestrator.run in the job queue via the on_step callback. Preserves progress across crashes, restarts and early terminations so a run continues from the current browser state. Otherwise every interruption discards the run and the agent repeats completed actions from scratch.

resilience.name: model-call retry with exponential backoff
resilience.what_it_is: Provider HTTP calls are retried on timeout, network error, HTTP 429 or 5xx with backoff MODEL_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS * 2^(attempt-1) (default 1s), up to MODEL_MAX_RETRIES + 1 attempts (default 3). Other 4xx fail immediately. Final failure raises ProviderAPIError with a retryable flag. The OpenAI host-bridge transport uses the same scheme.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps every adapter.decide model request inside one agent step. Absorbs transient provider and network failures before they reach the orchestrator. Otherwise one rate-limit or network hiccup turns the step into 'error' and ends the run.

resilience.name: forced structured output with decision schema validation
resilience.what_it_is: Every provider path constrains the model to the BrowserActionDecision JSON schema (OpenAI forced strict function tool, Claude forced tool_choice, Gemini responseJsonSchema, CLI --json-schema/--output-schema). The result is validated by Pydantic with extra='forbid', field length limits and per-action requirements (click needs a target, type needs text, navigate needs a valid http(s) URL). Invalid output raises and the step ends with status 'error'; the error is logged and the run stops.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model response and _execute_decision. Guarantees that only a well-formed, complete single action reaches the browser. Otherwise malformed or incomplete model output executes as a wrong or undefined browser action.

resilience.name: tolerant decision parsing of CLI output
resilience.what_it_is: parse_decision_text tries three stages: direct schema validation of the text, recursive search for a valid decision object inside parsed JSON wrappers, and a scan of the raw text for embedded JSON objects via raw_decode.
resilience.function_in_system: Applied to CLI and host-bridge model output before execution. Recovers a valid decision from wrapper JSON or surrounding text emitted by agent CLIs. Otherwise output noise from the CLI fails the step although a valid decision is present.

resilience.name: prompt rules for risk labeling and self-escalation
resilience.what_it_is: The base planner prompt instructs the model to never invent URLs, elements or file paths, to always set a risk_category (read, write, upload, post, payment, account_change, destructive) and to return request_human_takeover for login, MFA, CAPTCHA, payments, sending/posting or uncertainty.
resilience.function_in_system: Part of every decide prompt in all workflow profiles. Makes the model classify the risk of each action and hand risky steps to a human. Otherwise hallucinated targets and risky actions reach the executor unlabeled. The label drives the approval gates (see risk-category approval gate).

resilience.name: risk-category approval gate for high-risk actions
resilience.what_it_is: execute_decision always calls require_decision_approval. approval_kind_for_decision maps risk_category post, payment, account_change and destructive, plus every upload (REQUIRE_APPROVAL_FOR_UPLOADS, default True), to an approval kind. If no approved approval_id matches, a pending approval is created or reused, an optional webhook is dispatched and ApprovalRequiredError is raised. An approval is bound to its session, its kind and the exact decision (all fields except reason and confidence), expires APPROVAL_TTL_MINUTES (default 15) after the decision and is single-use: mark_executed sets 'executed' and further transitions are refused. An identical pending request is reused.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the executor between the model decision and the Playwright operation, in every workflow profile. The step ends with status 'approval_required' and the run stops until a human approves. The trigger is the risk_category the model assigns itself (see prompt rules for risk labeling). Otherwise payments, posts, account changes and deletions decided by the model execute directly on the live site.

async def require_approved(
    self,
    *,
    approval_id: str,
    session_id: str,
    kind: ApprovalKind,
    action: BrowserActionDecision,
) -> ApprovalRecord:
    approval = await self.get(approval_id)
    if approval.session_id != session_id:
        raise PermissionError(f"approval {approval_id} does not belong to session {session_id}")
    if approval.kind != kind:
        raise PermissionError(f"approval {approval_id} does not cover {kind}")
    if approval.status != "approved":
        raise PermissionError(f"approval {approval_id} is not approved")
    self._ensure_not_expired(approval)
    if not self._actions_match(approval.action, action):
        raise PermissionError(f"approval {approval_id} does not match the requested action")
    return approval

async def mark_executed(self, approval_id: str) -> ApprovalRecord:
    async with self._lock:
        approval = await self.get(approval_id)
        if approval.status != "approved":
            raise PermissionError(f"approval {approval_id} is not approved")
        self._ensure_not_expired(approval)
        now = utc_now()
        approval.status = "executed"
        approval.updated_at = now
        approval.executed_at = now
        await self._persist(approval)
        return approval

async with self._lock:

resilience.name: per-action browser timeout
resilience.what_it_is: Every page gets a Playwright default timeout of ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS (default 15000 ms). After each operation _settle waits for networkidle at most min(action_timeout_ms, 5000) ms, then 250 ms, and proceeds when networkidle is never reached.

resilience.name: contract-bounded attempt retry loop with reflexion notes
resilience.what_it_is: A harness run executes the same TaskContract up to budget.max_attempts times; each attempt is one full orchestrator.run plus a verification pass. After every attempt that fails verification, a reflexion block listing the failed postconditions, the missing evidence and a next-mutation hint is appended to the run's strategy.md.
